page_notes.central: Saturnus named; nude bent gray-bearded man with long staff and sickle, star over groin, green ground within large ring.
page_notes.satellites: Capricorn-like horned animal at left; clothed water pourer at right; banner names Capricornus and urne as Saturn's domus.
page_notes.lower: Infancia label, red Metten label; two naked children with red balls in lower roundel.
page_notes.text: German declares Saturn harmful to living beings; several middle words uncertain. Latin top and ribbon describe Saturn and his houses. Small bottom Latin annotation refers to inferior figure, age/state and planet, but complete syntax unread.
page_notes.limits: Central old figure and lower infancy scene are different domains; no same-actor equation. No source image implies four seasons.

page_notes.central: Iupiter named; bearded nude crowned figure, bundle of arrow/lightning-like objects and knobbed staff.
page_notes.satellites: Archer and paired fish roundels; banner In Iovis domo Pisces simulque Chirona approximately readable.
page_notes.lower: Puericia and red Prime; young clothed male/female figures with tablet/board-like objects and a basket.
page_notes.text: German clear contrast approximately Was Saturnus übels tüt / Das bringet Iupiter ze güt, followed by Jupiter's children good/rich and holy/beautiful/personally phrased traits. Full Latin not diplomatically transcribed.
page_notes.limits: Contrast is written, but no measured individual intervention or particular Saturn event repaired by Jupiter. Bottom marginal Latin partly unread.

page_notes.central: Mars named; nude man in blue cap with spear/banner and shield, both with flame-like red motifs; star at groin.
page_notes.satellites: Ram left and scorpion right; horizontal ribbon Est Aries martis ... Scorpio ... gives two houses.
page_notes.lower: Age label uncertain, visually V...licias/Puerilitas?; red canonical-hour label approximately Terce. Clothed man raises club toward clothed woman, who raises hand.
page_notes.text: German links Mars's evil to being in his houses, his children to angry disposition, and their shedding human blood. Approximate lines So er in sinen husen stat / Sine kint ... zornigen mut / Sy vergiessent gern menschen blut.
page_notes.limits: Do not supply uncertain age from a canonical list; hostile act is depicted, but no detailed medical event or named victims.

page_notes.central: Sol named; nude crowned man with sceptre and orb, sun-face at groin.
page_notes.satellites: Lion repeated in both small satellite roundels. Ribbon approximately In leone Sol ... nec in alia hospitatur: explicit restriction to Leo, despite duplicated visual slots.
page_notes.lower: Adolescencia label; red Sexte. Seated male/female at round table with drinking/serving vessels; woman holds distaff, man holds round patterned item.
page_notes.text: Latin top describes Sun-born person and states Phoebus resides in Leo. German extols sun among planets and health-related effect, some words uncertain.
page_notes.limits: Two lion images do not imply two distinct Sun houses. Hour and age labels remain different semantic domains.

page_notes.central: Venus named; nude long-haired wreath-bearing woman, two-flowered stem in left hand, red rectangular mirror-like object with central disk/four corner disks in right; star at groin.
page_notes.satellites: Bull and scales; ribbon names Libra and Taurus with Venus.
page_notes.lower: Iuventus; hour approximately None. Young man plays string instrument; seated young woman holds leafy wreath/stem.
page_notes.text: German says Venus is Jupiter holt (favourably disposed/friendly); both give a joy-related result (exact middle words uncertain); children live with dancing, pipes and string play. Latin top characterizes Venus-born and gives Taurus/Libra.
page_notes.limits: Friendship/joint subject are textual, but a causal law from alliance to every child's act is not established. Flower-holder is explicitly Venus, not automatically Spring.

page_notes.central: Mercurius named; nude youth with hat, double-headed entwined staff, hanging purse/cloth-like object and red winged feet.
page_notes.satellites: Clothed seated maiden left; two nude figures right. Ribbon names twins and virgin.
page_notes.lower: Senium; red Vesper. Older clothed man with beads and woman, hands in devotional/expressive positions.
page_notes.text: German names houses maget und zwilling, ability to write/read, and mind full of wisdom. Latin says ... sub Mercurio generatus and qualities including Instabilis; other words uncertain.
page_notes.limits: Central youthful Mercury, zodiac twins/maiden and older lower pair are distinct roles. German/Latin nuance not silently harmonized.

page_notes.central: Luna named; nude long-haired woman holding curved horn and burning torch, crescent face at groin, small wheels under both feet.
page_notes.satellites: Two matching red lobster/crab-like Cancer figures. Ribbon explicitly restricts horned Moon to Cancer alone, approximately solum cancrum inhabita.
page_notes.lower: Senectus; red Complet. Elderly man in bed and a clothed woman beside him touching/gesturing near him.
page_notes.text: German explicitly calls Moon moist and cold; children differently shaped, followed by sickness/old-age words with unresolved syntax. Latin gives Moon-born traits and Cancer.
page_notes.limits: Same two visual satellite slots again represent one named house. Bedside woman is not labelled physician; no medical treatment inferred from pose.

page_notes.central: Grammatica, female allegorical figure chopping standing trees with axe; felled trunks, branches and timber in foreground.
page_notes.lower: Magister Priscianus labelled seated teacher at lectern/book, hand raised toward three cloud-like openings.
page_notes.text: Large German stanza about grammar teaching right arrangement of words is crossed with repeated red diagonal cancellation strokes; small red replacement/additional lines above remain partly unread. Lower Latin clearly links grammar preceding the arts and failure to reach arts without the prior requirement; exact middle wording uncertain.
page_notes.limits: Cancellation and replacement must remain separate witnesses/states; do not treat every large cancelled line as current accepted text. Wood preparation is visible; full building/learning analogy awaits remaining art pages.

page_notes.central: Retorica, female figure using broad axe/adze to work a long rough timber resting on supports; cut-off irregular strips visible, two trees behind.
page_notes.lower: Magister Tullius seated with open book at lectern, three cloud-like forms above.
page_notes.text: German says Rhetorica works/colours speech, removes the rough (das grop hin dan), and teaches words/meaning; two Roman-number groups are present but not securely transcribed. Latin concerns ratio dicendi and flore loquendi; full syntax uncertain.
page_notes.limits: Pruning/shaping image has a textual speech-work counterpart. No certainty that every visible piece is the identical tree from previous page.

page_notes.central: Loyca, woman with large two-handled auger drilling a wooden hub-like piece; three curved wooden segments with holes lie nearby.
page_notes.lower: Magister Aristoteles, seated teacher with open book, raised finger, three cloud-like forms.
page_notes.text: German explicitly concerns whether speech is true or false (Ob wor/falsch ... rede) and words/names; a comparison involving a wheel/rim-like object is partly unread. Latin says sisters/teachers work in vain without her and distinguishes truth from falsehood, with exact phrase uncertain.
page_notes.limits: Truth discrimination is not equivalent to rhetorical ornament. Auger/hub interpretation is visual, not an exact restored technical noun.

page_notes.native: Arismetrica/Arismetica title; upper German number-teaching verse with Boecius and numerical examples whose exact wording remains uncertain. Central female uses a slender rod at a completed spoked wheel. Latin beneath: Explico per numerum que sit proportio rerum; Divido multiplico subtraho simul et addo (provisional native transcription, arithmetic operations clear). Lower Magister Boecius seated with open book and raised hand, repeated cloud-form motif. Arithmetic operations are written; no worked numerical example established. Wheel construction continuity is visual, not explicit material identity.

Geometria title; upper German says measures what is measurable and makes figures, names Euclides; first objects and some intervening words uncertain. Central female sets large compass between wheel hub and rim. Latin measurement/figures and measuring spaces/lands, exact continuous transcription incomplete. Lower Magister Euclides with open book and raised hand, repeated cloud-form motif. Same wheel category with distinct geometric operation; identity as the very same artifact across leaves remains unproved.

Musica; upper German links singing/string play, interval names/numbers and Pythagoras, but full interval wording not confidently transcribed. Central female holds a wheel with bells and raised hammer-like striker. Latin second clause reads approximately Ex numeris colligo que vocalis sit proportio: numerical basis for vocal proportion is written, exact first clause uncertain. Lower Magister Pittagoras/Pythagoras with open book. Bell count is not a proved division of the art or planet count.

Astronomia; top German explicitly says planets are seven and mentions nature of their children, a planet remaining in its house, the fixed northern Polus Arcticus and heaven's course; intervening wording/scope not fully certain. Central woman uses large quadrant-like observational instrument toward a wheel containing five visible stars. Written seven planets must not be replaced by image star count. Lower crowned king Ptolomeus with open book; Latin sky/star-course verse, complete exact wording uncertain. Does not establish that all pictured wheel segments encode named planets.

Theology wagon synthesis. Upper German explicitly names Theology, holy Trinity/holy scripture and word becoming flesh without a man's agency; closes Als da schribet peter von Parise (provisional). Grammar, Rhetoric and Logic named on scrolls above three women physically pulling wagon ropes. Arithmetic at front, Astronomy behind, Music and Geometry at wheels; the wheel-side red Grammatica label is crossed through and replaced in black by Geometria. Crowned Sancta theologia sits in wagon holding a bearded face image; not newly identified as a particular relic. Lower left Magister Sentenciarum Magister Petrus Lombardus with raised whip/flail. Latin calls philosophy domina, exact continuous verse uncertain. Visual cooperation and culmination are explicit in depicted actions, but no text proved that a single actual piece of wood persisted through every prior page. Peter von Parise in upper verse must not silently be identified with the separately captioned Peter Lombard.

Whole ending: concentric cosmos with Terra stat stil at center, Aqua/Aer/Ignis and seven named planet bands; periods written for planets while elemental bands say continuing movement/all time or without number. Clearly readable examples Jupiter xii iar, Mars ii iar, Sol ein iar..., exact fractional day/hour values not transcribed or normalized. Four blowing heads labeled Orient (upper left), Auster (upper right), Boreas (lower left), Occident (lower right), outside cloud perimeter. No cardinal north-up assumption; different domain from seven planetary agents or arts. Lower labeled sanctus Albertus magnus as bishop/master with open book and teaching gesture. Latin encomium and German scroll praise great Albert's learning/wisdom, some words uncertain. Whole published end is owned; subsequent catalogued blank244r/v not viewed and no URL guessed.
